title: Spec: replace per-column tight_bounds with file-level tight_stats in v4
summary: anoopj called a vote on the V4 spec change in PR #18585 that replaces the per-column tight_bounds field with a single file-level tight_stats flag on the tracked file. Under the change, tightness is tracked once per file and covers all statistics (bounds and null, NaN and value counts), so metadata-only queries can trust the counts as well. When the flag is absent, readers must assume stats are not tight. A deletion vector no longer implicitly makes stats wide: tight_stats is the authoritative indicator, and engines may retighten stats without rewriting data files. The vote was open for 72 hours. Thirteen replies were all +1; anuragmantri added that the change also applies well to column updates. The bundle contains no message announcing the result.

positions.stance: Stats tightness should be tracked once per file with a tight_stats flag covering bounds and counts, with absence meaning not tight and deletion vectors no longer implying wide stats.
Votes +1 and notes the change applies nicely to column updates too.

outcome.note: No result message is in the thread. The messages show 13 +1 votes, nine marked binding and four non-binding; no -1 votes.

why_it_matters: If adopted, V4 writers and readers use one per-file flag to decide whether all of a file's statistics can be trusted, and engines can retighten stats without rewriting data.
